evidence_boundaries.mechanistic_law: Establishes that the classical isovector E1 selection rule B(E1; Delta T = 0) = 0 breaks down systematically as Z increases along the N=Z line: in 100Sn (Z=50), Coulomb isospin mixing alpha_C^2 surges to 8.1%, inducing forbidden E1 transitions (B(E1) ~ 1.2x10^-3 W.u.) and generating a 1.4 MeV Coulomb spreading width in the GDR; this completely invalidates macroscopic isospin splitting formulas derived from neutron-rich nuclei (208Pb) where isospin impurity is suppressed by 1/(T0+1) to < 0.9%.
